subject: Planning: on-prem cluster sizing, node pools, and archival tier for AuroraEdge
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@auroraedge.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@auroraedge.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem cluster: sizing, node-pool mix, and long-term archive lanes

Karthik —

Thanks again for taking time. We are starting our internal planning for the AuroraEdge private deployment (on-prem in our primary DC). A few high-level constraints:

- Two racks in primary DC: mixed CPU+NVMe nodes and a smaller GPU rack for inference burst.
- Workloads: real-time inference (latency SLO 50ms P95), offline batch retraining, and long-term model/artifact archival (cold).
- Regulatory: encrypted-at-rest required; archival retention policy 7 years (rare reads).
- Network: east-west latency target under 1ms within cluster; egress windows limited to nightly maintenance for backup.

Can you help us with: cluster sizing options (three scenarios), node pool recommendations (CPU/GPU/ephemeral NVMe), persistent storage strategy (fast block for KV, slower encrypted object for cold), and an operational playbook for air-gapped bootstrap + occasional outbound windows?

We also need a short list of procurement lead times (e.g., NVMe models that work well) because we need to align with hardware ordering.

Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Infrastructure
AuroraEdge

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@auroraedge.io>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster: sizing, node-pool mix, and long-term archive lanes

Daniel —

Appreciate the context. I sketched three scenario buckets and attached an Excel that lays out assumptions (CPU hours, P95 tokens/sec, PV sizing, and archival throughput): low-footprint (pilot), production baseline, and production+high-availability (multi-rack failure domain). Please see auroraedge-cluster-scenarios-v2.xlsx attached.

High-level recommendations:
- Node pools:
  * control-plane: 3x small CPU nodes (separate mgmt network) protected by HSM/KMS for encryption keys;
  * inference-frontend (latency-optimized): 6–10 CPU+NVMe nodes with 1–2x local NVMe per pod for KV cache (use a write-through caching layer to persistent block store);
  * GPU-pool: 2–4 GPUs (NVIDIA A30/A100 class depending on model footprint) with graceful-preempt priority and eviction policies so batch jobs do not impact low-latency lane;
  * batch/worker: 4–8 CPU nodes attached to object-backup egress windows.
- Storage:
  * Fast PVs: encrypted block (Ceph/Rook or vendor SAN) for model artifacts and stateful pods; prefer LVM on top of NVMe for local caching;
  * Cold: encrypted object store (on-prem S3-compatible) with lifecycle rules to move to tape/archival slice after 90 days;
  * Backup cadence: incremental snapshots nightly during egress window; full snapshot weekly (outside business hours).
- Networking:
  * Dedicated management VLAN for control-plane and KMS traffic; data plane in separate VLANs with explicit ACLs;
  * BGP for rack-level routing, with ECMP for east-west; prioritize QoS for inference ports;
  * Egress gating: single egress jump host under your control for uploads (signed presigned URLs) and for vulnerability scanning during maintenance windows.
- Air-gapped bootstrap:
  * Provide 'bootstrap bundle' (OCI images + Helm charts + root CA) as a signed tarball you can import; we will provide a verification script and SHA checksums.

I want to loop Laura for networking constraints and Monica for backups/DR details. Two quick questions up front:
1) Do you have an on-prem S3-compatible endpoint today, or will we stand that up as part of this engagement?
2) What are expected average per-second inference requests at peak?

Next steps: propose a 60m technical review this week to walk the spreadsheet and the SVG network sketch.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: auroraedge-cluster-scenarios-v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@auroraedge.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@auroraedge.io>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster: sizing, node-pool mix, and long-term archive lanes

Daniel, Karthik —

Adding a few network-specific constraints we commonly see that affect PV placement and archival throughput:

- Avoid mixing backup traffic with low-latency inference networks; we recommend a physically separate 10G link or at minimum separate fiber pairs and VLANs for backup/archival traffic.
- If you plan to use local NVMe for KV cache, ensure persistent logging/metrics export happens over the management network to protect data-plane bandwidth.
- For encryption key availability in air-gapped mode: we recommend a small HA key proxy cluster in your mgmt VLAN (2 nodes) that caches key material for short TTLs rather than relying on frequent external KMS calls. That reduces outbound requirements during normal operations.

Operational playbook (short):
1) Bootstrap (air-gapped): signed bundle import -> control-plane bring-up -> apply network ACLs -> validate PVs and node taints.
2) Validation: synthetic P95 latency test for inference lane (target <50ms) and archival write test (target sustained 300MB/s to object store during egress window).
3) Failover drills: simulate one-rack loss and validate model rehydration from cold snapshot within 2 hours.

I've dropped a simple network sketch in networking-pod-to-storage-lane.svg and flagged a couple of QoS knobs in the spreadsheet.

Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: networking-pod-to-storage-lane.svg (svg)]

Subject: Re: On-prem cluster: sizing, node-pool mix, and long-term archive lanes

Karthik / Laura —

Thanks — this looks like exactly what we needed. A couple clarifications from procurement and security:

- We do not have an S3-compatible endpoint today; procurement will order a private object store (Dell ECS or MinIO) as part of phase 1. Lead time for Dell quoted at ~8 weeks.
- Peak inference: we expect 220 requests/sec sustained (spiky bursts to 500 rps) during business hours; average request size small (few hundred tokens).
- Encryption: must use customer-managed keys via our HSM (YubiHSM) and we need an offline key provisioning step.

Can you put the HA key proxy suggestion and the offline key provisioning steps into a short 'security appendix' we can hand to our InfoSec? Also useful would be a short bullet list of recommended NVMe SKUs (endurance class) and typical procurement lead times.

We are available for a technical review Friday (16th) afternoon PST.

Priya
Head of Platform Engineering
AuroraEdge
